Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 61, verses 1–3:

It is Medinan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} This is an explanation of His greatness, His dominion, and the submission of all things to Him, blessed and exalted is He, and that all who are in the heavens and the earth glorify Allah with His praise, worship Him, and ask Him for their needs. {And He is the Almighty}: the One who subdues things by His might and authority. {the Wise}: in His creation and His command.

{2–3} {O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?} That is: why do you say good things and urge others toward them, while you may praise yourselves for them though you do not do them, and forbid evil while you may declare yourselves free of it though you are stained by it and characterized by it? Is this blameworthy state fitting for the believers? Or is it among the greatest hatred in the sight of Allah that a servant says what he does not do? For this reason, the one who commands good should be the first of people to hasten to it, and the one who forbids evil should be the farthest of people from it. Allah, the Exalted, said: {Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves, and you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?} And Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said [to his people]: {And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from.}

Then will you not reason?} And Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said [to his people]: {And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from.}

{4} This is an exhortation from God to His servants to engage in jihad in His cause, and an instruction to them on how they should act: they should line up in jihad in a solid, compact row, level, without any gap occurring in the ranks. Their rows should be in an orderly arrangement by which equality among the mujahideen, mutual support, striking terror into the enemy, and encouraging one another are achieved. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) would attend a battle, he would arrange his companions in rows and position them in their stations such that no one would rely on another; rather, each group among them would be concerned with its own position and would be fulfilling its duty. In this manner, tasks are completed and perfection is attained.

{5} That is: {And when Moses said to his people}, rebuking them for their conduct and reproaching them for harming him, though they knew that he was a messenger of God: {Why do you harm me}, by words and deeds, {when you know that I am the messenger of God to you}? The messenger has the right to be honoured, esteemed, obeyed in his commands, and promptly complied with in his judgments. As for harming a messenger whose benefit to creation surpasses every benefit after the benefit of God, it is the utmost in insolence, audacity and deviation from the straight path, which they knew and abandoned. Therefore He said: {So when they deviated}, that is, turned away from the truth by their own intention, {God caused their hearts to deviate}, as a punishment for their deviation, which they had chosen for themselves and were content with. God did not grant them success in guidance, because good does not befit them and they are fit only for evil. {And God does not guide the defiant people}, that is, those for whom defiance has never ceased to be a attribute, who have no intention toward guidance. This noble verse indicates that God's misguidance of His servants is not an injustice on His part, nor is it an argument against Him; rather it is due to a cause on their part, for they are the ones who shut the door of guidance upon themselves after they had recognised it. Then He requites them with misguidance, deviation and the turning of their hearts as a punishment for them and as justice from Him toward them, as He, exalted is He, said: {And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly}.

{6} God, exalted is He, says, reporting on the obstinacy of the earlier Children of Israel, whom Jesus son of Mary called, saying: ﴿O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you﴾; that is: God sent me to call you to good and forbid you from evil, and He strengthened me with manifest proofs. And among what indicates my truthfulness is that I am ﴿confirming what was before me of the Torah﴾; that is: I came with what Moses brought of the Torah and the divine laws. Had I been a claimant to prophethood, I would have come with other than what the messengers brought. And [I am] ﴿confirming what was before me of the Torah﴾ also in that it gave news of me and gave glad tidings, so I came and was sent confirming it. ﴿And bringing glad tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾: he is Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet of the Hashim clan. So Jesus, peace be upon him, like all the prophets, confirms the prophet before him and gives glad tidings of the prophet who follows him, unlike the liars, who utterly contradict the prophets and oppose them in their attributes, morals, commands and prohibitions. ﴿Then when he came to them﴾: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom Jesus foretold, ﴿with clear proofs﴾; that is: the evident evidences showing that he is indeed he, and that he is truly the Messenger of God. ﴿They said﴾: being obstinate against the truth and denying it: ﴿This is manifest magic.﴾ This is one of the most astonishing wonders: a Messenger whose mission has become clear and more evident than the midday sun is called a plainly evident sorcerer. Is there any greater abandonment than this? And is there any more eloquent slander than this slander, which negates from him what was known of his mission and attributes to him what was furthest from him?

{7} ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God?﴾ Whether with this or with something else, while he has no excuse and his argument has been cut off, because he ﴿is being called to Islam﴾: and it is made clear to him with its proofs and evidences. ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾: those who continue steadfast in their wrongdoing, whom no admonition turns back, and whom no clarification or proof restrains, especially these oppressors who stand against the truth in order to repel it and to support falsehood.

{8} For this reason God said of them: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾; that is: with the corrupt statements that issue from them, by which they repel the truth, and which have no reality, but rather increase the discerning person in knowledge of the falsehood they are upon. ﴿But God will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it﴾; that is: God has undertaken to support His religion and to complete the truth with which He sent His messengers, and to manifest His light in all regions, even though the disbelievers dislike it and expend, out of their dislike of it, everything they are capable of by which they might reach the extinguishing of God's light. For they are overcome, and their likeness is like that of one who blows on the sun with his mouth to extinguish it; they have achieved neither their aim, nor has their reason been spared from deficiency and defect.

{9} Then He mentioned the cause of the manifestation and victory of the Islamic religion, both material and spiritual, saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾; that is: with beneficial knowledge and righteous action, knowledge that guides to God and to the abode of His honour, guides to the best deeds and morals, and guides to the benefits of this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And the religion of truth﴾; that is: the religion by which one is indebted and worships the Lord of the worlds, which is truth and sincerity, with no deficiency in it and no flaw afflicting it. Rather, its commands are nourishment for hearts and spirits and rest for bodies, and abandoning its prohibitions is safety from evil and corruption. Therefore what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with of guidance and the religion of truth is the greatest proof and evidence of his truthfulness, and it is an enduring proof as long as time endures; whenever the intelligent person reflects upon it more, he increases in joy and insight. ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾; that is: that He may elevate it above all other religions by argument and proof, and make its adherents who uphold it prevail by the sword and the spear.

As for the religion itself, this attribute is inherent in it at all times, so no contender can contend against it or dispute with it without it prevailing over him and overcoming him, and it attains supremacy and dominance. As for those who ascribe themselves to it: when they uphold it, are illumined by its light, and are guided by its guidance in the interests of their religion and their worldly life, then likewise no one can stand against them, and they will certainly prevail over the adherents of other religions. But if they neglect it and are content with mere affiliation to it, that will not benefit them, and their neglect of it becomes the cause of enemies being given power over them. Whoever surveys the circumstances and considers the early and later Muslims will know this.

{10} This is an admonition, guidance and direction from the Most Merciful of the merciful to His believing servants, toward the greatest trade, the most noble sought-after goal, and the highest desired thing, by which one attains deliverance from the painful punishment and triumph in everlasting bliss. He used the particle of offering (ʿard), which indicates that this is a matter every aspiring person desires and every intelligent person aspires to.

{11} It is as if it was said: "What is this trade that has such a status?" So He said: ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. It is well known that complete faith is the firm affirmation of what Allah has commanded to be affirmed, which necessitates the actions of the limbs, the most noble of which is jihad in His cause. Therefore He said: ﴿and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives﴾, by expending your souls and your lives in confronting the enemies of Islam, with the aim of supporting the religion of Allah and raising His word, and by spending what you can of your wealth in that sought-after objective. Although that is disliked by souls and burdensome to them, it is ﴿better for you, if you only knew﴾. For in it is worldly good: victory over the enemies, honor that is the opposite of humiliation, abundant provision, and expansion and relief of the breast. And there is otherworldly good: triumph in the reward of Allah and deliverance from His punishment.

{12} For this reason He mentioned the reward in the Hereafter, saying: ﴿He will forgive you your sins﴾, which includes both minor and major sins, for faith in Allah and jihad in His cause expiate sins, even if they are major sins. ﴿And admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾; that is, beneath their dwellings, palaces, upper chambers and trees flow rivers of water that does not change, rivers of milk whose taste does not alter, rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink it, and rivers of purified honey, and for them therein is every kind of fruit. ﴿And pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence﴾; that is, they combine every goodness of loftiness, elevation, fine construction and adornment. So much so that the people of the upper chambers among the people of ʿIlliyyin are seen by the people of Paradise just as a bright star is seen on the eastern or western horizon. And so much so that the building of Paradise is partly of bricks of gold and partly of bricks of silver, its tents are of pearls and coral, and some of its dwellings are of emerald and jewels of various colors, of the finest hues. So much so that, because of their clarity, its exterior is seen from its interior and its interior from its exterior. In it is goodness and beauty beyond the description of any describer, and beyond what has occurred to the heart of any of the worlds. They cannot conceive of it until they see it and enjoy its beauty, and their eyes are delighted by it.

In that state, were it not that Allah created the people of Paradise and brought them into existence in a complete state that does not accept non-existence, they would nearly die of joy. Glory be to the One whom none of His creatures can enumerate in praise, rather He is as He has praised Himself, and above what any of His creatures can praise Him. Blessed is the Majestic, the Beautiful, who created the abode of bliss and placed in it such majesty and beauty as dazzles the minds of creation and captivates their hearts. Exalted is He who possesses perfect wisdom, of which is that if He showed the servants Paradise and they looked at its bliss, none would remain behind from it, and this life in this troubled abode, whose bliss is mixed with its pain and whose joy with its sorrow, would not be pleasant to them. Paradise was named "Gardens of ʿAdn" because its people dwell in it permanently; they never leave it, and they never desire any change from it. That is the great reward and the beautiful recompense, the supreme triumph, for which there is no triumph like it. This is the otherworldly reward.

{13} As for the worldly reward of this trade, He mentioned it with His words: ﴿and another [favor] you love﴾; that is, another quality you will obtain which you love, namely: ﴿help from Allah and an imminent victory﴾ over the enemies, by which honor and joy are attained, and by which the circle of Islam expands and abundant provision is attained. This is the reward of the believing mujahidin. As for believers other than the fighters, when others have undertaken jihad, Allah, exalted is He, does not cause them to despair of His bounty and His kindness; rather He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾; that is, of the immediate and deferred reward, each according to the measure of his faith, even if they do not reach the level of those who strive in the cause of Allah. As the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger, Paradise becomes obligatory for him." Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, the narrator of the hadith, was amazed by it and said: "Repeat it to me, O Messenger of Allah!"
